_label: MEASURED -- real Verilator RTL cosimulation of the full top-level datapath, not estimated
test: rtl/experimental/fp_div/tb_top_verilator_variant.cpp (shared across baseline/B1/B2/B3, compiled 7 ways: baseline, B1, B2, B3 at REORDER_DEPTH 1/2/4/8)
scope: 1,110,000 transactions per variant (200,000 per single-mode stage x4 + 100,000 mixed-mode + 3 x 70,000 adversarial-pattern stages: dense long Q4_0-encode burst, dense alternating Q4_0-encode/Q8_0-encode, dense random-mode), randomized valid/ready backpressure in the non-dense stages, 4 reset-safety stages (mid-stream flush, reset while Q4_0 encode divider busy, reset while queues non-empty [B3 only], all four preceding stages checked for 0 fails before any per-mode stage begins), id/mode/data checked every retirement against exact C quantizer golden vectors, 200,000-cycle-of-no-progress deadlock watchdog active throughout (never triggered)
note_on_scale_vs_phase_b2_committed_numb: This workload (1,110,000 txn, includes 3 dense adversarial stages) is DELIBERATELY larger and harsher than phase-b2.md's own committed 520,000-txn number -- task item 6 for this phase asks for >=1,000,000 transactions plus adversarial patterns specifically. Both B2 and baseline/B1 were re-run against this SAME new, larger workload here (not reused from the old 520k run) so every per-mode mean-latency number in this file is directly comparable across all 7 variants -- do not compare these B2 numbers to phase-b2.md's own 22.842-cycle Q8_ENC figure, which was measured against a smaller, less adversarial workload.

b1.note: byte-identical to baseline at this granularity, as expected -- B1 only changes q4_scale's constant-divisor path.

b2.note: reproduces phase-b3-root-cause.md's diagnosis: full serialization while any Q4_0 encode is in flight (q4enc_inflight gates ALL issuance) is the sole cause of the ~2.1-2.6x collateral slowdown on the three untouched fixed-latency chains.

b3_depth1.verdict: WORSE than B2 on every metric -- the uniform +1-cycle reorder-buffer tax applies to every transaction while REORDER_DEPTH=1 provides no real concurrency window (it degenerates to almost the same full-serialization behavior B2 already has, since only 1 transaction can ever be outstanding), so this depth is strictly dominated by B2 itself.

b3_depth2.verdict: Still WORSE than B2 on every metric. Better than depth=1 but the concurrency window (2 slots, one permanently occupied by whichever Q4_0 encode is in flight) is too small relative to this workload's Q4_0-encode frequency to offset the added buffering latency.

b3_depth4.verdict: First depth to BEAT B2: overall cycles/transaction -4.03% vs B2 (10.936 vs 11.395), Q8_ENC collateral slowdown -7.9% (2.376x vs 2.580x), Q8_DEC/Q4_DEC collateral slowdown ~-1.5%. Depth-bound stall (6.75%) is now small relative to the structurally-unavoidable Q4_0-divider-busy stall (81.33% of all cycles), meaning most of the remaining stall is no longer a scheduling artifact.

b3_depth8.verdict: Marginal further improvement over depth=4 (overall cycles/transaction -0.73% vs depth=4, -4.73% vs B2). Q8_DEC/Q4_DEC collateral slowdown drops below 2x for the first time (1.987x, 1.971x). Depth-bound stall is now only 1.08% of all cycles -- almost all remaining stall (81.96%) is the structurally-unavoidable single-divider-busy cost, confirming diminishing returns beyond this depth.

reset_while_queues_non_empty_b3_only.b3_depth1: pass, 0 fails, outstanding correctly returned to 0
reset_while_queues_non_empty_b3_only.b3_depth2: pass, 0 fails, outstanding correctly returned to 0

reset_while_queues_non_empty_b3_only.b3_depth8: pass, 0 fails, outstanding correctly returned to 0

deadlock_watchdog: 200,000-cycle no-progress bound, active on every stage of every variant, never triggered (0 occurrences across 7 x 1,110,000 = 7,770,000 transaction-checks)
